la:adj:matutinus.html:
mātūtīnus, a, um, adj.
Matuta; cf.: mane, manus, maturus
,
of or belonging to the morning, morning- (class.): tempora,the morning hours,: frigora,: dies,the morning,: equi, i. e. Aurorae,: radii,the morning sun,: somni,: harena,i. e. the morning-hunt in the Circus,: cliens,who comes early in the morning,: Juppiter,who is saluted early in the morning,: Aeneas se matutinus agebat,was up early,: pater, i. e. Janus, who (as the god of time) was invoked early in the morning, that he might promote business, : ter matutino Tiberi mergetur,: matutino sudans amomo,.—
Transf.: frons,i. e. sober, serious,.— Subst.: mātūtīnum, i, n., the morning, morning-, : serere matutinis, meridie metere,.— Hence, adv., in two forms.
mātūtī-nē, in the morning, early in the morning, only ap. P.—
mātūtīnō, early in the morning (post-Aug.), , 53, 54, § 181; 19, 12, 60, § 183; ; , p. 198 al.; cf. P.; P.

la:noun:mater.html:
māter, tris, f.
root ma-; Sanscr. and Zend, to make, measure, like Gr. μήτηρ, the maker, akin with Dor. μάτηρ; Germ. Mutter; Engl. mother; cf.: materies, manus
,
a mother (dat. sing. matre, Corp. Inscr. Lat. 177; dat. plur. matris, : matrabus,).
Lit.: si quidem istius regis (sc. Anci Martii) matrem habemus, ignoramus patrem,: cur non sit heres matri suae?: de pietate in matrem,: Sassia mater hujus Aviti,: Hecate, quae matre Asteria est,who has Asteria for her mother,: musa, matre nati,: mater esse de aliquo, to be a mother, i. e. to be pregnant by any one, : facere aliquam matrem,: mater familias or familiae, the mistress of a house, matron (v. familia).—
Transf., a nurse: mater sua ... quae mammam dabat, neque adeo mater ipsa, quae illos pepererat,: puero opust cibo, opus est autem matri quae puerum lavit, 10: lambere matrem,.—As a title of honor, mother, applied to priestesses: jubemus te salvere, mater. Sa. Salvete puellae, : amice benigneque honorem, mater, nostrum habes,.—To goddesses: Vesta mater,; : mater Matuta, v. h. v.: Flora mater,; the same: florum,: mater magna, or absol.: Mater, i. e. Cybele, the mother of all the gods: matris magnae sacerdos,; cf. absol.: matris quate cymbala circum, ; : secreta palatia Matris,: matres ... cives Romanae, ut jus liberorum consecutae videantur,: matris condicionem sequi,; cf. §§ 67, 86.—Also, in gen., a woman, a lady; usu. in plur., women, ladies: pilentis matres in mollibus,: matres atque viri,; cf. .—Of the earth, as the mother of all: exercitum Dis Manibus matrique Terrae deberi,; cf. .—Of a country: haec terra, quam matrem appellamus,: amorum,i. e. Venus,: cupidinum,i. e. Venus,.—Of animals: porci cum matribus,: excretos prohibent a matribus haedos,: ova assunt ipsis cum matribus, i. e. cum gallinis,: mater simia,: pullus hirundinis ad quem volat mater,.—Of the trunks of trees, etc.: plantas tenero abscindens de corpore matrum,; .—Of a fountain, as the source of waters: ex grandi palude oritur (fluvius), quam matrem ejus accolae appellant,.—Of a chief or capital city: mater Italiae Roma,: ut Graeci dicere solent, urbium mater, Cydona,: (Cilicia) matrem urbium habet Tarsum,; cf. Metropolis.—
Trop.
The mother, i. e. maternal love: simul matrem labare sensit,: mater redit, Sen. ap. Med. 928.—
Motherhood, maternity, .—
A producing cause, origin, source, etc. (freq. and class.): apes mellis matres,: mater omnium bonarum artium sapientia est,: philosophia mater omnium bene factorum,: avaritiae mater, luxuries,: voluptas, malorum mater omnium,; ; ; ; ; ; : juris et religionis,: justitiae imbecillitas mater est,: intemperantia omnium perturbationum mater,: similitudo est satietatis mater,: utilitas justi prope mater et aequi,; ; .—Comically: eam (sc. hirneam) ego vini ut matre fuerat natum, eduxi meri,i. e. as it came from the cask, without the addition of water,.—
The protector, shelter, home: urbs Roma, virtutum omnium mater, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 5, 3, 1: illa Jerusalem quae est mater nostra,.

la:adj:maturus.html:
mātūrus, a, um (
sup. usually maturissimus; less freq. maturrimus,; cf. the adv.), adj.
root, Sanscr. ma-, measure, time, whence mane, matutinus; cf.: manus, modus; hence, timely, ready in time
, ripe, mature (class.).
Lit., of fruits: poma matura et cocta (opp. cruda),: uva,: fruges,: maturissimae ficus,.—With dat.: seges matura messi,ripe for harvesting,.—Neutr. as subst.: quod maturi erat (opp. viride),. —
Transf.
Ripe, mature, of the proper age, proper, fit, seasonable, timely, etc.—With dat.: filia matura viro,ripe for marriage, marriageable,: maturus bello,: vitulus templis maturus et arae,old enough for sacrifice,: virgo,: ovis,fit for bearing,: Roxane matura ex Alexandro,; cf. venter,ripe for delivery, ready to bring forth,: infans,: aetas,mature, fit for action,: progenies matura militiae,: L. Caesar viris, of the proper age for assuming the toga virilis, .—Piur. subst.: mātūri, adults (opp. pueri), : omnia matura sunt, victoria, praeda, laus,ready to be seized,.—With ad: ad arma,.—Of mental qualities: ipse enim Thucydides, si posterius fuisset, multo maturior ac mitior fuisset,: annis gravis atque animi maturus Aletes,mature in judgment,: aevi,ripe in years,: centuriones,who had served out their time,: imperia,old, antiquated,: scribendi tempus maturius,more seasonable, more favorable,: mihi vero ad nonas bene maturum videtur fore, just

at the right time, : se maturam oppetere mortem,in good old age,: senex,.—

Powerful, vigorous: glaebasque jacentis Pulverolenter coquat maturis solibus aestas,: lux,: ignes (anni),: maturae mala nequitiae,full-grown depravity,.—
That takes place early, early, speedy, quick: mittam hodie huic suo die natali malam rem magnam et maturam,: matura faba, the early bean (opp. to the late bean), : satio (opp. to late sowing),: fenum, the first hay (opp. to the after-math), : hiemes,early,: decessio,: honores,: judicium,quick,: robur aetatis quam maturrimum precari,: aetas maturissima,early life,: si mora pro culpa est, ego sum maturior illo,was there earlier,.—Hence, adv.: mātūrē (sup. maturissime and maturrime; v.the foll.).
Seasonably, opportunely, at the proper time (class.): custodes mature sentiunt,: satis mature occurrit,: ubi consulueris, mature facto opus est,—
Betimes, early, speedily, quickly, soon: mature fieri senem,: proficisci,: Romam venire,.— Comp.: maturius proficiscitur,: maturius pervenire,: tempus quam res maturius me deserat,: maturius ad Epulas ire,: voluerunt veteres maturius hereditates adiri,.—Sup.: maximos tumultus maturissime disjeci, Cato ap. P.: res maturissime vindicanda est,as quickly, as early as possible,: quippe qui omnium maturrime ad publicas causas accesserim,: perge qua coeptas, ut quam maturrime merita invenias, Dietsch.: quibus rebus quam maturrime occurrendum putabat,—
Prematurely, untimely: pater mature decessit,.—With a play upon the three meanings of the word (A., B., and C.): qui homo mature quaesivit pecuniam, Nisi eam mature parsit, mature esurit,he who has made money at the right time, if he is not soon sparing of it, will too soon suffer hunger,.

Mătĭus, a,
the name of a Roman gens. So, Cn. Matius, a poet and translator of the Iliad, ; ; Müll.; perh. the same with C. Matius,a friend of Cæsar and Cicero,; ; ; ; —Hence,
Mătĭā-nus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to a Matius, Matian: mala,a kind of apple,; ; : poma,; Minutal,.

la:noun:maturitas.html:
mātūrĭtas, ātis, f.
id.
.
Ripeness, maturity (class.).
Lit.: frugum,: neque multum a maturitate aberant (frumenta),; frumentorum,fin.: celerius occidere festinatam maturitatem,an accelerated, precocious maturity,.—
Transf., the full or proper time for any thing, perfection, ripeness, maturity: maturitates gignendi,: ad maturitatem perducere,: pervenire,: maturitatem adipisci,: partūs,: aestiva, fullness of heat, Cic. ap. (Rep. 4, 1, 1 B. and K.): muriae,i. e. its proper strength,: aetatis ad prudentiam,: ejus rei maturitas,: habere maturitatem suam,: maturitatem Galli criminando,mental maturity, ripe understanding,; so, veteris imperatoris,: indeflexa aetatis,.—In plur.: temporum maturitates, mutationes, vicissitudinesque,the maturing of the seasons,; ; but: si maturitas temporum, expectata foret, the full time, when the supplies would be exhausted, .—*
Concr., ripe fruit, .—
Gentleness, mildness (late Lat.), .—
Promptness, expedition (post-Aug.): poenae,: maturitatem beneficio Caesaris praestare,to hasten,.

la:verb:maturo.gloss: to ripen, make ripe, bring to maturity
senses: to ripen, make ripe, bring to maturity
la:verb:maturo.html:
mātūro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
id.
.
Act., to make ripe, ripen, to bring to ma turity (class.).
Lit., of fruits: uvas,: pomum,. —Pass.: maturari, to grow ripe, ripen, to come to maturity: frumenta maturantur,: omnia maturata,ripened,: uva maturata dulcescit,ripe,.—
Transf., to make ripe, to ripen, mature, soften, bring to maturity: vitis alba suppurationes veteres maturat,: lupini strumas maturant,: partus conceptos,: olivas muria,to make ripe, soft, eatable,.—Pass., to become ripe or soft, to come to maturity: ova in sicco maturari,: alumen aestivis solibus maturatur,: concoctione maturata,.—
Trop., to hasten, accelerate, quicken, despatch, expedite (class.).
With acc.: domum ad coepta maturanda redire jubet,: iter,: mortem alicui,: necem alicui,; cf.: mortem ea res maturat,: insidias consuli,: fugam,: negotia,: sibi exitium,: maturatur recordatio,: spem praedae suae morte maturare,.—
With inf., to make haste or hasten to do a thing: jube maturare illam exire huc,: flumen Axonam exercitum transducere maturavit,: ab urbe proficisci,: venire,: iter pergere,.—
To hurry too much, precipitate: ni Catilina maturasset signum dare,had not Catiline given the signal too soon,: jussis ceteris quantum possent maturare sequi,.—
Poet.: multa quae mox caelo properanda sereno, maturare datur,i. e. to do in good time, betimes,.—
Neutr.
Lit., to grow ripe, ripen (post-class.): ficus, quae sero maturant,: tardius,.—
Transf., to make haste, hasten (rare but class.): successor tuus non potest ita maturare, ut, etc.,: legati in Africam maturantes veniunt,: et maturavit Romanus, ne, etc.,: maturandum ne, etc.,: facto maturatoque opus esse,; cf. : quam maturato opus erat,.—Hence, adv.: mātūrātē, betimes, quickly (very rare): properare,; also: mātūrātō, hastily (late Lat.), Schol. Verg. ap. Clan. Auct. Mai. vol. 7, p. 291.

la:noun:matrimonium.html:
mātrĭmōnĭum, ii, n.
mater
,
wedlock, marriage, matrimony.
Lit. (class.): ire in matrimonium,i. e. to be married,: in matrimonium dare, opp. in concubinatum,: alicujus tenere, to be one's spouse: te Q. Metelli matrimonium tenuisse sciebas,: in matrimonium dare alicui filiam suam,to give in marriage,: in matrimonium ducere alicujus filiam,to marry,: in matrimonium petere sibi aliquam,to ask in marriage,: in matrimonium collocare,to give in marriage,: in matrimonium collocare (filiam),; : locare in matrimonio stabili et certo,to take in marriage, marry,: matrimonio uxorem exigere,to put her away, repudiate her,; so, matrimonio exturbare,: dimittere aliquam e matrimonio,to put her away, to repudiate, divorce her,: justum matrimonium est, si, etc.,lawful marriage,: non justo contractum,.—
Transf., in plur., married women, wives (post-Aug.): matrimonia et pecudes hostium praedae destinare,; : severius matrimonia sua viri coercerent,; ; : matrimonia a finitimis petita,.

la:adj:maternus.gloss: of or pertaining to a mother, maternal
senses: of or pertaining to a mother, maternal
related through the mother, or her side of the family
la:adj:maternus.html:
māternus, a, um, adj.
mater
,
of or belonging to a mother, maternal (class.): sanguis, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 184 Vahl.): paternus maternusque sanguis,: animus,: nomen,: menses,the months of pregnancy,: tempora,time of pregnancy,: Caesar cingens maternā tempora myrto, i. e. of Venus, the mother of Æneas, from whom sprang the race of the Cæsars, : arma (Aeneae),i. e. which his mother Venus had obtained for him from Vulcan,: aves,i. e. the doves sacred to Venus,: avus,i. e. Atlas, the father of Maia, the mother of Mercury,: Delum maternam invisit Apollo,i. e. where his mother Latona had borne him,: aequora, i. e. from which she (Venus) was born, : Numa,related by the mother's side,; cf.: an ad maternos Latinos hoc senatus consultum pertineat,: nobilitas,by the mother's side,: Idus, i. e. of May (Mercury's birthday), 5—Of animals: ut agnus condiscat maternum trahere alimentum,: perdix materna vacans cura,.

la:noun:matrona.gloss: married woman, wife or matron, especially of an honorable man
senses: married woman, wife or matron, especially of an honorable man
la:noun:matrona.html:
mātrōna, ae, f.
id.
,
a married woman, wife, matron (whether she was in manu or not; consequently more general in its application than mater familias, which always denoted one who was in manu).
In gen.: matronam dictam esse proprie, quae in matrimonium cum viro convenisset, quoad in eo matrimonio maneret, etiamsi liberi nondum nati forent: dictamque esse ita a matris nomine non adepto jam sed cum spe et omine mox adipiscendi: unde ipsum quoque matrimonium dicitur; matrem autem familias appellatam esse eam solam, quae in mariti manu mancipioque, aut in ejus, in cujus maritus, manu mancipicque esset: quoniam non in matrimonium tantum, sed in familiam quoque mariti, et in sui heredis locum venisset, and 9: convocatis plebeis matronis,.—Only rarely of a married woman, woman in general: ut matronarum hic facta pernovit probe,: quae (dea) quia partus matronarum tueatur,; cf.: et fetus matrona dabit, * : cum prole matronisque nostris,: tyranni,: matronae muros complent, Enn. ap. Serv ad (Ann. v 376 Vahl.): tum muros variā cinxere coronā Matronae, * : matronae tacitae spectent, tacitae rideant

: matronas prostratae pudicitiae,: dilectae adulter matronae,.—

Esp.
The word very early acquired the accessory idea of (moral or social) dignity, rank. Matronae is thus used even by Ennius of women of quality, ladies: matronae opulentae, optimates, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 294 Vahl.); cf., in like manner, in Plautus: ubi istas videas summo genere natas Summates matronas,; so Cicero applies to the noble women carried off from the Sabines the term matronae,: matrona laris,the lady of the house,.—
With the accessory idea of estimable, virtuous, chaste, etc.: nominis matronae sanctitudinem, Afran. ap. : eam hic ornatam adducas ad matronarum modum, Brix ad loc.; cf.: matronarum sanctitas,: VETERIS SANCTITATIS MATRONA,. So opp. meretrix, ; cf. ; : ut matrona meretrici dispar erit atque Discolor,; : matronae praeter faciem nil cernere possis, etc.,: capitis matrona pudici,.—
Hence, an appellation of Juno: hinc matrona Juno (stetit),: MATRONIS IVNONIBVS,; and of other protecting goddesses of places, (But not of vestals; v. Drak. ad .)

măthēmătĭcus, a, um, adj., = μαθηματικός,
of or belonging to mathematics, mathematical (class.).
Adj.: mathematica nota,: artes,: cogitatio,: disciplinae,i. e. geometry, arithmetic, astronomy, music, geography, optics,.—
Subst.
Măthēmătĭcus, i, m.
A mathematician, ; id. Ac. 2, 36, 116; ; .—
An astrologer (post-Aug.): mathematici, genus hominum potentibus infidum, sperantibus fallax, quod in civitate nostra et vetabitur semper et retinebitur,: nota mathematicis genesis tua,; : qui de salute principis ... mathematicos consulit, cum eo qui responderit, capite punitur,.—
Măthēmătĭca, ae, f.
Mathematics, ; v. l. mă-thēmătĭcē ( = μαθηματική, sc. τέχνη).—
Astrology: addictus mathematicae, persuasionisque plenus, cuncta fato agi,.

la:verb:maturesco.html:
mātūresco, rŭi, 3,
v. inch. n. [maturus], to become ripe, ripen, to come to maturity (class.).
Lit., of fruits: cum maturescere frumenta inciperent,; : fructus maturescens,.—
Transf.: partus maturescunt ... novem lunae cursibus, * : nubilibus maturuit annis, ripened to marriageable years, i. e. a marriageable age, : libros opinabar nondum satis maturuisse,: si virtutes ejus maturuissent,had come to maturity, to perfection,.

la:noun:materia.html:
mātĕrĭa, ae (
gen. materiāi, ), and mātĕrĭes, ēi (only in nom. and acc. sing., and once gen. plur. materierum, ; v. Neue, Formenl. 1, p. 383), f.
from same root with mater, q. v.
, stuff, matter, materials of which any thing is composed; so the wood of a tree, vine, etc., timber for building (opp. lignum, wood for fuel); nutritive matter or substance for food (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: materia rerum, ex qua et in qua sunt omnia,; cf. : materiam superabat opus,: materiae apparatio,: rudis,i. e. chaos,; cf.: omnis fere materia nondum formata rudis appellatur, Cinc. ap. Paul. ex Müll.: (arbor) inter corticem et materiem,: crispa,: materiae longitudo,: vitis in materiam, frondemque effunditur,: si nihil valet materies,: in eam insulam materiam, calcem, caementa, atque arma convexit,: caesa,; cf. ; : cornus non potest videri materies propter exilitatem, sed lignum,: materiae, lignorum aggestus,: videndum est ut materies suppetat scutariis,: proba materies est, si probum adhibes fabrum,: imprimebatur sculptura materiae anuli, sive ex ferro sive ex auro foret, . —Plur.: deūm imagines mortalibus materiis in species hominum effingere,.—Of food: imbecillissimam materiam esse omnem caulem oleris, sqq.; cf. of the means of subsistence: consumere omnem materiam,; matter, in gen.: materies aliqua mala erat,.—In abstract, matter, the material universe: Deus ex materia ortus est, aut materia ex Deo,.—
Esp., matter of suppuration, pus, .—
Transf., a stock, race, breed: quod ex vetere materia nascitur, plerumque congeneratum parentis senium refert,: generosa (equorum), —
Trop.
The matter, subjectmatter, subject, topic, ground, theme of any exertion of the mental powers, as of an art or science, an oration, etc.: materiam artis eam dicimus in qua omnis ars et facultas, quae conficitur ex arte, versatur. Ut si medicinae materiam dicamus morbos ac vulnera, quod in his omnis medicina versetur; item quibus in rebus versatur ars et facultas oratoria, eas res materiam artis rhetoricae nominamus,: quasi materia, quam tractet, et in qua versetur, subjecta est veritas,: est enim deformitatis et corporis vitiorum satis bella materies ad jocandum,; ; ; : sermonum,: materies crescit mihi, my matter (for writing about) increases, : rei. : aequa viribus,a subject suited to your powers,: infames,: extra materiam juris,the province,.—
A cause, occasion, source, opportunity (cf. mater, II.): quid enim odisset Clodium Milo segetem ac materiam suae gloriae? (for which shortly before: fons perennis gloriae suae): materies ingentis decoris,: non praebiturum se illi eo die materiam,: major orationis,: criminandi,: omnium malorum,: materiam invidiae dare,: materiam bonitati dare,: scelerum,: seditionis,: laudis,: benefaciendi,: ne quid materiae praeberet Neroni,occasion of jealousy,: epistolae, quae materiam sermonibus praebuere,: praebere materiam causasque jocorum,: materiamque sibi ducis indulgentia quaerit,.—
Natural abilities, talents, genius, disposition: fac, fuisse in isto C. Laelii, M. Catonis materiem atque indolem,: in animis humanis,: materiam ingentis publice privatimque decoris omni indulgentia nostra nutriamus,: ad cupiditatem,; .—Hence, one's nature, natural character: non sum materia digna perire tua,thy unfeeling disposition,.—
A subject, argument, course of thought, topic (post-Aug.): tertium diem esse, quod omni labore materiae ad scribendum destinatae non inveniret exordium,: argumentum plura significat ... omnem ad scribendum destinatam materiam ita appellari,: video non futurum finem in ista materia ullum, nisi quem ipse mihi fecero,: pulcritudinem materiae considerare,; : materiam ex titulo cognosces, al. (materies animi est, materia arboris; et materies qualitas ingenii, materia fabris apta, Mai.; but this distinction is not observed by class. writers).
